'''Charles Cameron Woodson''' (born October 7, 1976) is an American former professional <!-- Per NFL player page policies, should say former when a player retires, not retired. Leave as former --> [[American football|football]] player in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for 18 seasons with the [[Oakland Raiders]] and [[Green Bay Packers]]. He spent his first 14 seasons at [[cornerback]] and his final four as a [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]]. Woodson played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]], twice earning [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors. As a junior in 1997, he was a [[College football national championships in NCAA Division I FBS|national champion]] and the first primarily defensive player in college football history to win the [[Heisman Trophy]].

Selected fourth overall by the Raiders in the [[1998 NFL draft]], Woodson received [[Pro Bowl]] selections during his first four seasons and two first-team [[All-Pro]] honors. Woodson left the Raiders after eight seasons to join the Packers, where he played his next seven seasons. During his Packers tenure, Woodson was named [[National Football League Defensive Player of the Year Award|Defensive Player of the Year]] in 2009 and won [[Super Bowl XLV]], while extending his Pro Bowl selections to eight and his first-team All-Pro honors to four. He returned to the Raiders for his last three seasons, earning his ninth Pro Bowl selection in his final season.

One of the NFL's most decorated players, Woodson is tied with [[Rod Woodson]] (no relation) and [[Darren Sharper]] for the most defensive touchdowns, second in interceptions returned for touchdowns, and tied with [[Ken Riley]] for the fifth-most interceptions. He is also one of the few players to appear in a Pro Bowl during three different decades. Woodson was inducted to the [[College Football Hall of Fame]] in 2018 and the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] in 2021. He became a [[limited partner]] of the [[Cleveland Browns]] in 2025.

'''Charles Benjamin Rogers''' (May 23, 1981 – November 11, 2019) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] for three seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State Spartans]], earning [[unanimous All-American]] honors and recognition as the top college wide receiver in the country. He played [[college football]] for the [[Eastern Michigan Eagles football|Eastern Michigan Eagles]]. He was selected by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the second round of the [[1998 NFL draft]] and played 15 seasons in the NFL, most of it as a backup with his hometown [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], with whom he earned two [[Super Bowl ring]]s ([[Super Bowl XL]] and [[Super Bowl XLIII]]).<ref>{{Cite web |title=1998 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1998/draft.htm |access-date=March 29, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Batch currently works for [[KDKA-TV]] in [[Pittsburgh]] as a pre-game analyst for the Steelers as well as a [[color commentator]] for their [[National Football League preseason|preseason]] games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 5, 2015 |title=Former Steelers Charlie Batch and Chris Hoke join KDKA-TV broadcasts |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/former-steelers-charlie-batch-and-chris-hoke-join-kdka-tv-broadcasts-15249134 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211204210035/https://www.steelers.com/news/former-steelers-charlie-batch-and-chris-hoke-join-kdka-tv-broadcasts-15249134 |archive-date=December 4, 2021 |access-date=August 14, 2022 |website=www.steelers.com |language=en-US}}</ref> In addition, he co-hosts the Steeler Post-Game Show on WDVE Radio. Batch also works with Champs Sports Network as a color analyst for [[Western Pennsylvania Interscholastic Athletic League|WPIAL]] high school football and basketball broadcasts.

'''Charles Anthony Tillman'''<ref name="MON">{{Cite web |title=Profile |url=http://www.rostermon.com/player/1703/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180127203518/http://www.rostermon.com/player/1703/ |archive-date=January 27, 2018 |access-date=July 19, 2016 |website=rostermon.com}}</ref> (born February 23, 1981), nicknamed "'''Peanut'''",<ref name="Till-NFLPlayers">Donnelly, Mike, [http://www.nflplayers.com/news/news_release.aspx?id=6202 Charles Tillman - Not Your Typical 'Peanut'] (January 18, 2007), nflplayers.com, Retrieved on July 25, 2007.</ref> is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns football|Louisiana–Lafayette Ragin' Cajuns]], and was selected by the [[Chicago Bears]] in the second round of the [[2003 NFL draft]].

Tillman played 12 years for the Bears, helping them reach [[Super Bowl XLI]], and also played one year with the [[Carolina Panthers]], making [[Super Bowl 50]] with the team, although he had been placed on [[injured reserve]] earlier in the season. He was selected to two [[Pro Bowl]]s and was the [[Walter Payton Man of the Year]] in 2013.

He was known for his cover skills as well as his ability to force fumbles by stripping or "punching" the ball away from an opponent with a well-timed technique commonly known as the "[[Peanut Punch (football)|Peanut Punch]]".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg |first=Jon |date=2014-09-16 |title=Greenberg: Tillman's Peanut Punch historic |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/11534600/charles-tillman-peanut-punch-historic-chicago-bears |access-date=2024-07-02 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/17114030/the-art-charles-tillman-peanut-punch-nfl-chicago-bears-carolina-panthers|title=The art of Charles Tillman's 'Peanut Punch'|work=ESPN |date=July 20, 2016 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2172511/2020/10/31/charles-tillman-nfl-bears-peanut-punch/|title=Remembering Charles Tillman's NFL-changing 'Peanut Punch' with the Bears|work=The Athletic |last1=Jahns |first1=Adam }}</ref> After retiring from the NFL, Tillman was an [[FBI agent]] from 2018 to 2025.

'''Charles Brown''' (born October 29, 1958) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for six seasons. Thielemann]].<ref>{{cite news| url = https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1985/08/27/redskins-trade-brown-for-thielemann/8c548f2a-b530-4402-84ac-c2e6916317bb/| title = Redskins Trade Brown for Thielemann - The Washington Post| newspaper = [[The Washington Post]]}}</ref> He was nicknamed "Good ol' Charlie Brown" in reference to the eponymous comic strip character.

He played [[college football]] at [[South Carolina State University]] and was selected in the eighth round of the [[1981 NFL draft]]. Brown played wide receiver and defensive back for the [[Washington Commandos]] of the [[Arena Football League]] in 1990.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1990/06/16/charlie-brown-back-on-field-of-dreams/5c919cfa-d2f8-4b34-931a-bcc238f327fa/ | title=CHARLIE BROWN BACK ON FIELD OF DREAMS | work=Washington Post | date=June 16, 1990 | accessdate=February 3, 2024 | author=Sheinin, Dave}}</ref> He was slated to be a receiver for the Washington Marauders of the [[Professional Spring Football League]] in 1992, but the league never got off the ground.

Brown was [[head coach]] of the [[Savannah High School (Georgia)|Savannah High Blue Jackets]] ([[Savannah, Georgia]]) of the Savannah Chatham County Football League. He is currently wide receivers coach of Marlboro County High School Bulldogs varsity football team in [[Bennettsville, South Carolina]].
